entry.title: Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United: "I don't think he was anybody's first choice"

media:group.media:title: Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United: "I don't think he was anybody's first choice"
media:group.media:description:
Mauricio Pochettino has called Sir Alex Ferguson the best manager in the history of football, and Ferguson reportedly wanted him to succeed José Mourinho at Manchester United in 2018 (90min). Joseph says on The ARCHV podcast that the fit has always been there.
He also points to Tottenham Hotspur, where Pochettino went through transfer windows without a signing under chairman Daniel Levy. How he got the job doesn't worry Joseph either: "I don't think he was anybody's first choice. He kind of never is." He thinks that could help, because "this is an opportunity that he's always wanted".
Recorded on Thursday 12 November 2026, the day before the club confirmed Pochettino as head coach.
Should Manchester United's board back Pochettino's plan?

entry.title: Can Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United surprise Liverpool at Anfield?

media:group.media:title: Can Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United surprise Liverpool at Anfield?
media:group.media:description:
Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United play Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday 22 November 2026, and The ARCHV podcast's Joseph thinks Pochettino has an advantage Liverpool do not.
He took charge on 18 November, so Anfield is his first game, against a Liverpool side with one home league win in five this season.
Joseph recorded this three days before kick-off, on a solo episode of The ARCHV podcast.

entry.title: Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox: is Manchester United's recruitment a mess?

media:group.media:title: Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox: is Manchester United's recruitment a mess?
media:group.media:description:
Manchester United's recruitment problems land on Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Joseph tells Coach Mo (@coachmo_pdcst) on The ARCHV podcast. His case is wingers and strikers who don't fit one system, signings who are always injured, and a process he says is "failing at every single step".
His fix is to lean on director of recruitment Christopher Vivell, who came from Red Bull Salzburg (Sky Sports). "You guys don't know what you're doing," he says of Berrada and Wilcox. Recorded on Friday 13 November 2026, the day the club confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as head coach.
Berrada and Wilcox: keep or change?

entry.title: Manchester United's mentality: the hardest thing Mauricio Pochettino has to fix

media:group.media:title: Manchester United's mentality: the hardest thing Mauricio Pochettino has to fix
media:group.media:description:
Manchester United's mentality is the hardest thing Mauricio Pochettino has to fix, Joseph tells Coach Mo (@coachmo_pdcst) on The ARCHV podcast. He means a pattern over the last five or six years rather than one match: "we go up early in the game 2-0 and by the end of the game we've lost 3-2".
The shape and the pressing come second, and he expects Pochettino and his staff to solve those. One correction to what he says: Pochettino has managed three English clubs (Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea), not two.
Recorded on Friday 13 November 2026, the day Manchester United confirmed Pochettino as head coach.
Pochettino's first fix at Manchester United: mentality or tactics?

entry.title: David de Gea Saves for Manchester United in the Premier League, Ending at Arsenal in 2017

media:group.media:title: David de Gea Saves for Manchester United in the Premier League, Ending at Arsenal in 2017
media:group.media:description:
David de Gea made 14 saves for Manchester United at Arsenal on 2 December 2017, level with the Premier League record for one match, and Manchester United won 3-1 at the Emirates Stadium, finishing with ten men after Paul Pogba's red card. A low stop at his near post from that night closes this Short.
It starts at Stamford Bridge on 5 February 2012. Manchester United had come back from 3-0 down to 3-3 against Chelsea when Juan Mata bent a free kick at the top corner in stoppage time, and De Gea got his fingertips to it.
The middle save is from St James' Park on 27 December 2021, a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United. He took 70 per cent of the club's man of the match vote.

entry.title: Diogo Dalot "often lets us down": does Mauricio Pochettino need a new Manchester United right back?

media:group.media:title: Diogo Dalot "often lets us down": does Mauricio Pochettino need a new Manchester United right back?
media:group.media:description:
Diogo Dalot gets Joseph's respect, "so much respect for him", but his verdict on The ARCHV podcast is blunt: "in moments in games, Diogo Dalot often lets us down". He wants Manchester United to bring in a right back, ideally in January.
Dalot was taken off after 66 minutes against Aston Villa on 8 November 2026 (ESPN). The rest of Joseph's January list is cover at left back if there is no backup, and a striker who plays almost every game. Benjamin Šeško is expected to be out with a shin injury until the New Year (ESPN).
Recorded on Thursday 12 November 2026, the day before the club confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as head coach.
New right back in January?

entry.title: Mauricio Pochettino's £7.4m release clause: should Manchester United have hired him in the summer?

media:group.media:title: Mauricio Pochettino's £7.4m release clause: should Manchester United have hired him in the summer?
media:group.media:description:
Mauricio Pochettino's release clause cost Manchester United about £7.4m (Sky Sports, BBC Sport), and he had only signed his new U.S. Soccer contract in August 2026. Joseph thinks United could have had him in the summer if the due diligence had been done.
He traces it back on The ARCHV podcast: Ruben Amorim's last weeks, his reported fallout with Jason Wilcox, Michael Carrick's start, and a summer window he says left the squad short. Recorded on Thursday 12 November 2026, the day Carrick was sacked and the day before the club confirmed Pochettino.
Summer or November: when should Manchester United have hired Pochettino?

entry.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Champions League Goals for Manchester United at Arsenal and AS Roma

media:group.media:title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Champions League Goals for Manchester United at Arsenal and AS Roma
media:group.media:description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice for Manchester United at the Emirates Stadium on 5 May 2009, a free kick after 11 minutes and a counter-attack finish after 61 minutes. The 3-1 UEFA Champions League semi-final second-leg win over Arsenal sent the club to the final in Rome.
The run starts with a header a year earlier, from a Paul Scholes cross at the Stadio Olimpico on 1 April 2008, in a 2-0 quarter-final first-leg win over AS Roma. Then the counter at Arsenal, which Ronaldo started with a backheel to Park Ji-sung before Wayne Rooney set him up, and the free kick closes it.

entry.title: Lionel Messi Against Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur: His 2018 Champions League Goals

media:group.media:title: Lionel Messi Against Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur: His 2018 Champions League Goals
media:group.media:description:
Lionel Messi scored five UEFA Champions League goals for FC Barcelona against Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur in 2018, and three of them are in this Short.
The first came at Stamford Bridge on 20 February 2018 in a 1-1 draw in the round of 16 first leg, and it was his first goal against Chelsea. In the second leg at Camp Nou on 14 March he scored twice in a 3-0 win, and the second of those, like the first through Thibaut Courtois's legs, was his 100th in the competition. That one closes the Short.
At Wembley Stadium on 3 October 2018 he scored twice against Tottenham Hotspur in the group stage, in the 56th and 90th minutes, as FC Barcelona won 4-2. The 90th-minute goal is the one here.

entry.title: Paul Pogba, Manchester United: Swansea City, Huddersfield Town, West Ham United, BSC Young Boys

media:group.media:title: Paul Pogba, Manchester United: Swansea City, Huddersfield Town, West Ham United, BSC Young Boys
media:group.media:description:
Paul Pogba scored 39 goals for Manchester United between 2016 and 2022, four of them against Swansea City, Huddersfield Town and West Ham United in the Premier League and BSC Young Boys in the UEFA Champions League.
At Swansea City on 6 November 2016 he opened a 3-1 win with a half-volley that Sky Sports put at 22 yards. On Boxing Day 2018 he scored twice against Huddersfield Town at Old Trafford, the second from 25 yards with 12 minutes left. Against West Ham United at the London Stadium on 5 December 2020, Bruno Fernandes rolled the ball into his path and he wrapped a shot into the top corner for 1-1, on the way to a 3-1 win. Lukasz Fabianski was in goal for Swansea City in 2016 and for West Ham United in 2020.
In Bern on 19 September 2018 he scored twice in a 3-0 Champions League group stage win over BSC Young Boys, the first after 35 minutes.

entry.title: Paul Scholes Goals: The Strike Against FC Barcelona That Sent Manchester United to Moscow

media:group.media:title: Paul Scholes Goals: The Strike Against FC Barcelona That Sent Manchester United to Moscow
media:group.media:description:
Paul Scholes scored the only goal of Manchester United's 2008 UEFA Champions League semi-final against FC Barcelona, 14 minutes into the second leg at Old Trafford on 29 April 2008. The first leg had finished 0-0, so that one strike put Manchester United in the final in Moscow.
Two Premier League goals come before it. Against Blackburn Rovers on 31 March 2007 he equalised after 61 minutes, and Manchester United went on to win 4-1. At Manchester City on 17 April 2010 he headed the only goal of the derby in stoppage time.
Manchester United drew 1-1 with Chelsea in the final at the Luzhniki Stadium on 21 May 2008 and won 6-5 on penalties.

entry.title: Will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick? Joseph says it's 50-50

media:group.media:title: Will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick? Joseph says it's 50-50
media:group.media:description:
Manchester United sacking Michael Carrick is a 50-50 for Joseph, who called it on The ARCHV podcast, recorded 8 November 2026 before Manchester United v Aston Villa in the Premier League.
Manchester United had won 1 of their first 9 Premier League games (W1 D4 L4, ESPN). Asked at his pre-match press conference whether he had been told outright he would be in charge next week, Carrick said, "No, I've just carried on as absolutely normal."
Footage: Manchester United press conference before Aston Villa, November 2026.
Sir Jim Ratcliffe or the Glazers: who should have the final say on Manchester United's manager?
